pr_title: REGR: Resampler.aggregate fails when used with column selection
pr_body:
- [x] closes #42905
- [x] tests added / passed
- [x] Ensure all linting tests pass, see [here](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing.html#code-standards) for how to run them
- [x] whatsnew entry

The method `resample._GroupByMixin._gotitem` calls

```
new_rs = type(self)(
    subset, groupby=groupby, parent=self, selection=selection, **kwargs
)
```

The selection (which ends up in kwargs in `__init__`) was being ignored.

issue_context.title: BUG: RecursionError using `agg` on a resampled SeriesGroupBy
issue_context.body:
- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

---

When you mix `resample` with `groupby` and try to use the `agg` method to supply multiple functions to either a DataFrameGroupBy or SeriesGroupBy, Python suddently exits without even raising an error.

I first thought I was running into this because I was supplying a single column expecting a DataFrame with multiple columns, but I can confirm this happens to me whether I provide a column (variable `b`) or apply the method to the entire GroupBy (variable `c`):

#### Code Sample

```python
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({
    'class': {
        0: 'beta', 1: 'alpha', 2: 'alpha', 3: 'gaga', 4: 'beta', 5: 'gaga',
        6: 'beta', 7: 'gaga', 8: 'beta', 9: 'gaga', 10: 'alpha', 11: 'beta',
        12: 'alpha', 13: 'gaga', 14: 'alpha'},
    'value': {
        0: 69, 1: 33, 2: 40, 3: 2, 4: 36, 5: 40, 6: 48, 7: 84, 8: 77, 9: 22,
        10: 55, 11: 82, 12: 37, 13: 88, 14: 41},
    'date': {
        0: pd.Timestamp('2021-02-28 00:00:00'),
        1: pd.Timestamp('2021-11-30 00:00:00'),
        2: pd.Timestamp('2021-02-28 00:00:00'),
        3: pd.Timestamp('2021-04-30 00:00:00'),
        4: pd.Timestamp('2021-02-28 00:00:00'),
        5: pd.Timestamp('2021-04-30 00:00:00'),
        6: pd.Timestamp('2021-07-31 00:00:00'),
        7: pd.Timestamp('2021-01-31 00:00:00'),
        8: pd.Timestamp('2021-01-31 00:00:00'),
        9: pd.Timestamp('2021-01-31 00:00:00'),
        10: pd.Timestamp('2021-04-30 00:00:00'),
        11: pd.Timestamp('2021-10-31 00:00:00'),
        12: pd.Timestamp('2021-09-30 00:00:00'),
        13: pd.Timestamp('2021-04-30 00:00:00'),
        14: pd.Timestamp('2021-05-31 00:00:00')}})

# This will exit Python
b = a\
    .set_index('date')\
    .groupby('class')\
    .resample('M')['value']\
    .agg(['sum', 'size'])

# Not informing a column will ALSO make Python exit
c = a\
    .set_index('date')\
    .groupby('class')\
    .resample('M')\
    .agg(['sum', 'size'])
```

#### Problem description

I'm not sure if this method is supported for instances of `DatetimeIndexResamplerGroupby` objects, but calling it without arguments is valid, giving:

```
<bound method Resampler.aggregate of <pandas.core.resample.DatetimeIndexResamplerGroupby object at 0x00000163B22B0100>>
```

Also, while the problem arises with either a Series or a DataFrame, given that using `agg` with multiple functions on a `SeriesGroupBy` will correctly create a DataFrame, I would expect the same to happen when resampling with timestamps:

```python
In [1]: a.groupby('class')['value'].agg(['sum', 'size'])
Out[1]:
       sum  size
class
alpha  206     5
beta   312     5
gaga   236     5
```

#### Expected Output

```

class date
alpha 2021-02-28   40     1
      2021-03-31    0     0
      2021-04-30   55     1
      2021-05-31   41     1

beta  2021-01-31   77     1
      2021-02-28  105     2
      2021-03-31    0     0
      2021-04-30    0     0
      2021-05-31    0     0
      2021-06-30    0     0
      2021-07-31   48     1
      2021-08-31    0     0
      2021-09-30    0     0
      2021-10-31   82     1
gaga  2021-01-31  106     2
      2021-02-28    0     0
      2021-03-31    0     0
      2021-04-30  130     3
```

review_comments: can this be done in stead in Resampler? this is quite low-level and _selection is note event defined here

_GroupByMixin is only used for (Datetime|Period|Timedelta)IndexResamplerGroupBy, so this change is localized.

It doesn't appear to me this can be moved to Resampler without quite a bit of hacking. The issue is that DatetimeIndexResamplerGroupby inherits both from _GroupByMixin and DatetimeIndexResampler, with _GroupByMixin first in the MRO. So currently, when constructing a new DatetimeIndexResamplerGroupby, the init of DatetimeIndexResampler (and hence, Resampler) never gets called.

Both _GroupByMixin and Resampler inits take a groupby argument, but they do not mean the same thing.  _GroupByMixin stashes groupby in `self._groupby` whereas Resampler in `self.groupby`. Moreover,  _GroupByMixin uses `parent.groupby` for `self.groupby`.

I've added _selection as an instance attribute via type-hints.
ok great. yeah this whole structure is not entirely great, but sounds good for now.
